name: @solana/kit
description: The modern Solana TypeScript SDK, successor to @solana/web3.js. Provides tree-shakeable, modular APIs for building, signing, and sending Solana transactions. Designed for modern JavaScript runtimes with improved TypeScript types and reduced bundle size. The active Solana SDK for new projects.

ecosystem_fit.notes: The modern replacement for @solana/web3.js. All new Solana TypeScript development should use @solana/kit.

trust_evidence.notes: Official Solana Labs SDK. The active migration target from @solana/web3.js. Used in all new Solana Foundation and Solana Labs TypeScript examples.

sdk_migration.notes: @solana/web3.js v1 is in maintenance mode — security patches only, no new features. @solana/kit is the official successor. Migration is HIGH risk: the API surface is entirely different (no direct method equivalents). Key changes: no more Connection class (replaced with Rpc client factory), Transaction replaced with transaction builder pattern, PublicKey replaced with Address type, Keypair replaced with CryptoKeyPair. New code should start with @solana/kit. Existing @solana/web3.js codebases require significant refactoring — plan 1-2 weeks for a non-trivial app. The Solana Foundation does not plan a compatibility shim.

scale_guidance.hackathon: Start new Solana hackathon projects with @solana/kit. The initial learning curve is steeper than @solana/web3.js, but the patterns are cleaner. Use Solana Foundation examples as references — they all use @solana/kit now.
scale_guidance.mvp: @solana/kit is the right choice for new Solana apps. The tree-shaking and TypeScript improvements are worth the migration cost for any greenfield project.
scale_guidance.production: Existing production apps on @solana/web3.js should plan a migration sprint. The risk is high but the long-term technical debt of staying on @solana/web3.js (no new features, potential security gaps) is worse than a planned migration.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: Helius provides a higher-level SDK for common Solana operations (token metadata, transaction helpers, webhook subscriptions). Use Helius alongside @solana/kit — Helius for data and events, @solana/kit for transaction construction.

anti_patterns: Starting new Solana TypeScript projects with @solana/web3.js@^1 — it is in maintenance mode. New projects should use @solana/kit.
Mixing @solana/web3.js and @solana/kit types in the same codebase — the types are incompatible. Complete the migration to @solana/kit before relying on it in production.
Assuming @solana/kit is a drop-in replacement — it is not. The entire API surface changed. Budget proper migration time.
